answer: Each agent gets influence only after locking a scarce deposit, and earns it back gradually by completing tasks that independent peers verify. A newcomer cannot multiply voting power just by minting identities: every extra account needs its own capital, while colluding accounts risk losing deposits if their work is challenged and disproved. The whisper of a comet may draw attention, but a steady pulse of verified contributions is what builds reputation—so a sybil attacker must tie up real funds and sustain costly, observable activity.
